$comment: AUTHORITY for the error codes a Semiont client reports. Every SDK generates its code types and its classifiers from this file, so a code means one thing in every language. TypeScript: scripts/spec/generate-error-codes.mjs writes packages/core/src/generated/error-codes.ts. A code belongs here only when something produces it: a member nothing emits promises a distinction the system does not make.

busRequest.docs: Why a bus request did not resolve. Some members restate a failure the answering peer declared on the wire (`wire` names its `CommandError.code`); the rest are facts only the requesting side knows, which is why this vocabulary and the wire's stay separate.

codes.docs: No reply arrived within the time the request allowed.
The peer answered with a failure whose code this vocabulary does not name, or that states none.
The bus stopped before a reply came: its client was disposed, or its transport closed.
The peer says this resource does not exist in its knowledge base.
THIS transport is not subscribed to the reply channel: a local misconfiguration, caught before emitting. Not to be confused with `bus.peer-unavailable`, which is the opposite end.
The service that answers this channel is not connected. Transient by nature, a peer still starting, and therefore the one failure on this list worth retrying.
The peer says this caller may not do what it asked: authenticated, not permitted. Retrying under the same credential cannot succeed, so a consumer surfaces it and never spins on it.
The peer declined and nothing went wrong: a `job:claim` found no pending job of the requested types. The one member a consumer parks on.

transport.docs: Transport-neutral failure vocabulary. Every transport maps its native failures to one of these, so a routing layer matches on the code without knowing the wire kind. Over HTTP the mapping is by status: `status` is an exact status, `statusFrom` every status at or above it.

codes.docs: Authentication is required: the token is missing or expired.
Authenticated, and lacking permission.
The resource is missing.
A concurrent modification, a duplicate, or another conflict with current state.
The request is malformed.
A limit refused it; the refusal's `Retry-After` says when to return.
The gateway is unreachable, the network failed, or the server answered 5xx.
A failure no other member names.

job.docs: Why a job its client follows ended without a result. A failure the queue will retry is not one of these: the job goes on, and its follower is told of the setback and keeps following.

codes.docs: The job failed and will not be tried again: the failure its worker reported, or the one its status states.
The job said nothing for longer than its follower allows. The follower has asked for it to be cancelled.

session.docs: Why a session itself is unusable. Per-request failures stay with their caller.

codes.docs: A session for the knowledge base could not be built or made ready.
The stored credential could not be validated at startup, for a reason other than the gateway refusing it.
The session could not be renewed: the issuer refused, or stayed unreachable until the retry budget was spent. Not a prompt to retry: retrying already happened.

signIn.docs: Why a person could not be signed in at the issuer a knowledge base trusts, or a session could not be renewed there. Over the authorization-code grant, the device grant, the refresh grant and revocation alike.

codes.docs: The knowledge base trusts no external issuer: there is nowhere to sign in.
The knowledge base did not say which issuer it trusts, or the issuer did not describe itself, or described another issuer, or offers no endpoint the grant needs.
A sign-in response arrived and no sign-in is pending here: it was completed already, or begun somewhere else.
The sign-in response does not belong to the pending sign-in.
The person, or the issuer, refused the sign-in.
The device code ran out before it was approved.
The sign-in was abandoned by whoever began it.
The issuer refused a token request, a device authorization or a revocation, or answered without what was asked for.

kbIdentity.docs: Why a knowledge base that was reached with a fresh sign-in could not be registered: it has to say who it is, and nothing stands in for its answer.

codes.docs: The knowledge base was not reached, so it said nothing.
The knowledge base answered that it cannot say what it is.
